Prevention: Bruchid-resistant varieties are available, such as
Remove and burn crop residues of the previous crop.
Harvest beans as soon as they mature.
Keep the bean store and the surrounding area clean.
Air dry the beans adequately before storage (ideal moisture level is 12%).
Disinfect old bags by immersing them in hot water (50°C-60°C) for 5 minutes.
Winnow and remove damaged and infested seed before storage.
Place the bagged beans on pallets.
Monitoring: Monitor bean pods at maturity to ensure timely harvesting.
Check inside the bean for larvae and pupae because they develop entirely inside.
Check for holed grains to identify bean bruchid larvae.
The larvae are white and are found in the tunnels which they create during feeding.
Inspect the storage facility and the surrounding area on a weekly basis.
Record all treatments done, on a stack card.
Bean treatment should be done soon after noticing less than 10 bruchids.
Repeat the treatment once the bruchids have resurfaced.
Direct Control: Use hermetic storage bags and clay pots for the storage of the beans.
Mix dried beans with ash (90g to 1kg of beans) or vegetable oil (5ml to 1kg of dried beans).
Treat the beans soon after harvesting, ensure that the grains have dried sufficiently before storing in polypropylene bags or hermetic storage facilities.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
